subject: History
stem: Choose the correct alternative and complete the sentence: The ______ saw the rise of Mathura School.
solution: Kushana period. The Mathura School of sculpture arose and flourished around Mathura under the Kushana rulers (roughly 1st to 3rd century CE). Its images were carved in the local spotted red sandstone and it produced some of the earliest anthropomorphic images of the Buddha, along with Jain and Brahmanical sculpture. The Gandhara School developed in the same Kushana age in the north-west, while the Gupta period is known for the later, more refined Sarnath style.

subject: History
stem: Choose the correct alternative and complete the sentence: Bhilar near Mahabaleshwar is known as the 'Village of ______'.
solution: Books. Bhilar, a strawberry-growing village near Mahabaleshwar in Satara district, was developed by the Government of Maharashtra in 2017 as 'Pustakanche Gaon', the Village of Books, on the model of Hay-on-Wye in Wales. Houses, schools, temples and hotels in the village were turned into open reading rooms holding thousands of Marathi books arranged subject-wise, so that visitors may read them free of charge. It promotes reading habit as well as literary tourism.

subject: History
stem: Choose the correct alternative and complete the sentence: According to ______, 'human history is the history of class struggle.'
solution: Karl Marx. In 'The Communist Manifesto' Marx and Engels declared that the history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggle. Marx held that the means of production and the resulting economic relations decide the structure of a society, that society is divided into the exploiting owner class and the exploited working class, and that the conflict between them is the driving force of historical change. This gave rise to Marxist historiography.

subject: History
stem: Identify the wrong pair in the following set and rewrite it: (i) Dashavatara - Tyagraj; (ii) Khanjiri Bhajan - Rashtrasant Tukdoji Maharaj; (iii) Keertan - Saint Namdev; (iv) Bharud - Saint Eknath.
solution: The wrong pair is (i) Dashavatara - Tyagraj. Corrected pair: Dashavatara - Folk theatre of the Konkan region (Sindhudurg and Goa). Dashavatara is a temple-festival folk drama built on the ten incarnations of Lord Vishnu; it has no connection with Tyagraj, who was a great composer-saint of Carnatic music in the south. The other three pairs are correct: Khanjiri Bhajan is associated with Rashtrasant Tukdoji Maharaj, Keertan with Saint Namdev, and Bharud with Saint Eknath.

stem: Identify the wrong pair in the following set and rewrite it: (i) James Mill - Feminist Historian; (ii) Friedrich Max Muller - Orientalist Scholar; (iii) Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade - Nationalistic Historian; (iv) Damodar Kosambi - Marxist Historian.

options.text: Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade - Nationalistic Historian

solution: The wrong pair is (i) James Mill - Feminist Historian. Corrected pair: James Mill - Colonialist (Imperialist) Historian. James Mill wrote 'The History of British India' (1817), in which he divided Indian history into the Hindu, Muslim and British periods and described Indian society as backward and in need of British rule; his writing is the classic example of colonial historiography, not of feminist historiography. The other three pairs are correct.

subject: History
subtopic: Applied History and Research in Various Fields
stem: Write a short note on: Sthalakosh.
solution: A Sthalakosh is a place-encyclopaedia, that is, a reference volume that compiles in one place all the available information about a particular locality, town or region. It records the geographical location and physical features of the place, the origin of its name, its history from ancient times to the present, its rulers and important events, its forts, temples, monuments and archaeological remains, its inscriptions and old documents, its festivals, fairs, crafts, occupations and folk traditions, and the notable persons connected with it. A sthalakosh is prepared by collecting oral accounts, old records, gazetteers, inscriptions and field observations, and by consulting local people. It is a valuable tool of applied history: it preserves local history that would otherwise be lost, helps students and researchers, guides the conservation of local heritage, and serves guides and tourists who visit the place.

subject: History
stem: Write a short note on: Orientalist Historiography.
solution: Orientalist historiography is the writing of the history of the East, especially of India, by European scholars known as Orientalists. It began in the second half of the eighteenth century when European scholars started studying Indian languages, religion, philosophy and literature. Sir William Jones founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal in 1784, studied Sanskrit and pointed out the kinship between Sanskrit, Greek and Latin. Friedrich Max Muller edited and translated the Rigveda and the 'Sacred Books of the East' series. These scholars translated ancient texts, deciphered old scripts, collected manuscripts and thus made the study of ancient India possible. However, orientalist writing also glorified only the ancient 'Hindu' past, treated India as unchanging and spiritual in contrast with the rational West, and its knowledge was often used to strengthen colonial rule. Even so, it laid the foundation of modern research in Indology and Indian history.

subject: History
stem: Write a short note on: The role of newspapers in the Indian struggle for independence.
solution: Newspapers were a powerful weapon of the Indian freedom struggle. They exposed the exploitative and repressive policies of British rule, carried news of national events to every corner of the country, and created public opinion and a feeling of nationalism among people who were scattered and largely unorganised. They educated readers about their rights, criticised social evils and supported reform, and mobilised people for movements such as the Swadeshi movement, the Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience and Quit India movements. Leaders themselves became editors: Lokmanya Tilak ran 'Kesari' and 'Maratha', Gopal Ganesh Agarkar 'Sudharak', Mahatma Gandhi 'Young India', 'Navjivan' and 'Harijan', Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar 'Mooknayak' and 'Bahishkrit Bharat', and Bhagat Singh and others also used the press. The government replied with repressive laws such as the Vernacular Press Act of 1878, and editors including Tilak were prosecuted and imprisoned. Newspapers of the period are therefore also an important source for writing the history of the freedom movement.

subject: History
stem: Explain the following statement with reasons: Foucault called his method, 'the archaeology of knowledge.'
solution: Michel Foucault, the French thinker and historian, rejected the traditional way of writing history as a smooth, continuous and chronological narrative of events. He held that every age has its own systems of thought, language and discourse which decide what counts as knowledge and truth in that age, and that these systems change abruptly rather than evolving in a straight line. Therefore the historian's task is not to tell a story of progress but to dig down through the accumulated layers of ideas, statements and discourses of a period and to expose the hidden rules and the relations of power that produced them. Because this is exactly what an archaeologist does when he digs through the strata of the earth to recover the buried past, Foucault called his method 'the archaeology of knowledge', and gave that title to his book of 1969.

subject: History
stem: Explain the following statement with reasons: It is necessary to preserve the tradition like Chitrakathi, which is on the verge of extinction.
solution: Chitrakathi is a very old form of picture storytelling in which episodes from the Ramayana, the Mahabharata and the Puranas are narrated with the help of a series of hand-painted pictures, accompanied by music on the ektari, huduk and cymbals. In Maharashtra it is kept alive by a few families of the Thakar community at Pinguli in Sindhudurg district, and the Paithan style of paintings belongs to the same tradition. It must be preserved because only a handful of families still practise it, and with no patronage, no steady income and the spread of television, cinema and mobile entertainment the younger generation is leaving the art, so it may die out altogether. Its paintings are a unique specimen of folk art and a valuable source for the study of folk life, costume, ornament and religious belief of past centuries; the tradition itself is a part of our intangible cultural heritage. Preserving it through documentation, museums, financial support, training and cultural tourism will keep this heritage alive and will also give the artist families a livelihood.

subject: History
stem: Explain the following statement with reasons: Toys can tell us about history.
solution: Toys are made out of the materials, tools, techniques and ideas that are available in their own age, and children play with miniature versions of the things they see around them. Therefore toys are material evidence of the past. Terracotta toys excavated from Harappan sites - bullock carts with movable wheels, whistles, spinning tops, rattles, marbles, figurines of humped bulls, elephants and monkeys and animal figures with movable heads - tell us about the transport, the domesticated animals, the technology of the potter's wheel, the toys and games and even the childhood of that civilisation. Toys and game materials found at other sites and in temple sculpture, such as dice, chess pieces and pieces used in games like chaupar, show us the games people played and their pastimes. The material used, whether clay, wood, ivory, cloth or metal, tells us about available resources, craft skills and trade, and the subjects of the toys reveal the beliefs, customs and social life of the time. So toys are an archaeological and material source for reconstructing history.

subject: History
subtopic: Management of Cultural and Natural Heritage
stem: Explain the following statement with reasons: The list of World Heritage Sites is announced by UNESCO.
solution: UNESCO, the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation, adopted the Convention concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage in 1972. Under this convention UNESCO is the international body responsible for identifying places which are of outstanding universal value to the whole of humanity and not merely to one nation. Member states nominate sites, the advisory bodies evaluate them against fixed criteria, and the World Heritage Committee of UNESCO takes the final decision and announces the World Heritage List, which contains cultural, natural and mixed sites. Inclusion in the list gives the site worldwide recognition, obliges the country concerned to conserve and protect it, makes technical guidance and money from the World Heritage Fund available for its conservation, gives it protection even in times of war, and greatly increases tourism. Ajanta, Ellora, the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Kaziranga and the Western Ghats are among the Indian sites on this list.

stem: Write in short about the contribution of Major Dhyan Chand in Olympics.
solution: Major Dhyan Chand was an expert hockey player who represented India at three successive Olympic Games and won a gold medal at each of them. He was a member of the Indian hockey teams that won gold at the 1928 and the 1932 Olympics, and in 1936 he led the team as captain at the Berlin Olympics, where India again won the gold medal. His outstanding ball control and goal scoring made India the unbeaten ruler of world hockey during those years and won the country international prestige in sport, which is why he is remembered as the 'Wizard of Hockey'. He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan in 1956, and his birthday, 29th August, is observed as National Sports Day in India.

subject: History
stem: Answer the following question in detail: What is feminist historiography?
solution: Feminist historiography means the re-writing and re-reading of history from the point of view of women. It grew out of the feminist movement of the twentieth century. Its main points are: (1) Traditional history was written by men and about men - about kings, wars, politics and administration - and women were almost completely left out of it; feminist historiography asks why this happened. (2) It re-examines the old sources and looks for new ones in order to bring out women's work, their place in the family and in production, motherhood, education, property rights and their contribution to social and political movements. (3) It shows that the difference between man and woman is not merely biological but is a social construction, that is, gender, and that the position of women changes from society to society and from age to age. (4) Simone de Beauvoir's book 'The Second Sex' (1949) gave the movement its philosophical base, and from the 1970s women's history became a recognised branch of study; Marxist and subaltern approaches also influenced it. In India it studies the condition of women in the past, the work of social reformers, and the participation of women in the freedom struggle. Thus feminist historiography completes history by restoring to it the half of society that had been ignored.

subject: History
stem: Answer the following question in detail: Why is library management important?
solution: A library is a storehouse of knowledge. It preserves books, periodicals, newspapers, rare manuscripts, maps, photographs, government reports and, today, digital and audio-visual material, and it makes them available to readers and researchers. Its management is important for the following reasons: (1) A library holds thousands of items, and unless they are classified and catalogued scientifically a reader cannot find the book he needs; proper cataloguing, indexing and shelf arrangement make the collection usable. (2) Old books, manuscripts and documents are fragile and are damaged by damp, dust, insects, fungus, light and careless handling; they need controlled temperature and humidity, chemical treatment, binding, lamination and digitisation, all of which need trained management. (3) The budget must be planned so that useful new books and journals are purchased and duplication is avoided. (4) Records of issue and return, membership, and security must be maintained so that books are not lost or stolen. (5) Reference service, reading rooms, e-resources and services for students, researchers and the visually handicapped have to be organised. (6) Modern libraries use computers, bar-coding, OPAC and networking, which require professionally trained librarians. Good management therefore keeps the accumulated knowledge of generations safe and within the reach of society, and library science also offers many professional opportunities.

subject: History
subtopic: Art, Applied Art and Professional Opportunities
stem: Answer the following question in detail: What kind of professional opportunities are available in the field of arts?
solution: The field of art offers a wide range of careers today. In the visual arts one may become a painter, sculptor, potter, or an artist working in metal, glass and textile design. In applied or commercial art there are openings in advertising, graphic design, illustration, book and magazine layout, packaging design, animation, video-game and web design, and photography. In the performing arts one may take up acting, singing, playing an instrument, dance and choreography, and behind the scenes there is scope for direction, script writing, set design, costume design, make-up, light and sound operation, editing and sound recording in theatre, cinema, television and the web. Museums, art galleries and archaeological departments need curators, conservators and restorers of art objects. Teaching is another wide field - art teachers in schools, and teachers in art schools, music and dance academies and universities. Art criticism and journalism, art history research, art management, gallery and auction work, and the running of one's own studio, handicraft or design business are further options. Formal training such as the B.F.A. and M.F.A. degrees, diplomas of drama, music and dance schools, and courses in animation and design prepare students for these careers, and heritage tourism and the entertainment industry are steadily increasing the demand for such professionals.

subject: History
stem: Answer the following question in detail: Write about the Dashavatara theatre.
solution: Dashavatara is one of the oldest and most popular folk theatre forms of Maharashtra. It is performed mainly in the Konkan, especially in Sindhudurg district, and in the neighbouring Goa, and the tradition is said to be about eight hundred years old. The performances are held at night in the precincts of a village temple during the annual festival of the deity, and they go on till dawn. The play opens with the worship of Ganapati along with Riddhi and Siddhi and of Goddess Saraswati; this introductory part is called the purvaranga, in which Sankhasur also appears. The main play that follows presents stories built around the ten incarnations, the dashavatara, of Lord Vishnu, and other tales from the Puranas and epics. There is no written script; the actors know the outline of the story and improvise their dialogues on the spot, which gives room for humour and topical comment. All the roles, including the female ones, were traditionally played by men. Bright and heavy make-up, wooden masks, crowns, ornaments and colourful costumes are used, and the harmonium, tabla or mridang and cymbals provide the music. Companies such as those of Walavalkar, Mochemadkar and Kalingan have kept the form alive, and it remains an important part of Konkan's cultural heritage.

subject: Political Science
stem: Choose the correct option and complete the statement: 73rd and 74th Amendment to the Indian constitution gave a constitutional status to ______.
solution: Local self-governing institutions. The 73rd Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to the rural local bodies, that is, the Panchayati Raj institutions of Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti and Zilla Parishad, and the 74th Amendment (1992) did the same for the urban local bodies, that is, Nagarpanchayats, Municipal Councils and Municipal Corporations. They made regular elections every five years compulsory, provided reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and women, and thus deepened democracy at the grass-roots level. The Vidhan Sabha, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha already had constitutional status from 1950.

subject: Political Science
subtopic: Challenges before Democracy at the Global Level
stem: Choose the correct option and complete the statement: The major challenge faced by all democratic nations in the world is ______.
solution: Deepening the roots of democracy. Holding elections and framing a constitution is only the beginning of democracy; every democratic country in the world faces the further task of making democratic values reach every institution and every citizen - strengthening local self-government, ensuring the participation of women and of weaker sections, making the administration transparent and accountable, and building tolerance and respect for opposition. This is called the deepening of democracy and it is the challenge common to all democratic nations. Religious conflict, naxal activity and the importance given to muscle power are challenges faced by particular countries, not by all of them.

subject: Political Science
stem: State whether the following statement is true or false and give the reason for your answer: Under special circumstances the Election Commission holds elections in a particular constituency for a second time.
solution: True. Ordinarily polling in a constituency is held only once on the day announced by the Election Commission. But the Commission is bound to secure a free and fair election, and in special circumstances it cancels the poll and orders a fresh poll, called re-polling, in the whole constituency or in the affected booths. Such circumstances are booth capturing, large-scale bogus voting or other malpractice, violence or rioting on polling day, the snatching or damaging of ballot boxes or electronic voting machines, a serious technical failure of the machines, or a natural calamity. If a contesting candidate of a recognised party dies before the poll, the election in that constituency is countermanded and held afresh. In these situations the election in that particular constituency is held for a second time.

subject: Political Science
stem: State whether the following statement is true or false and give the reason for your answer: Coalition politics leads to instability.
solution: True. A coalition government is formed when no single party wins a majority and several parties, often with different ideologies, programmes and regional interests, come together to run the government. Because the partners do not share a common outlook, they quarrel over the distribution of ministries and over policy; the smaller allies bargain and press their own demands and may threaten to walk out. If even one important partner withdraws its support, the government loses its majority and falls before completing its five-year term, and midterm elections become necessary. Decisions on important national policies get delayed or diluted because every step needs the consent of all the allies. India saw a number of short-lived governments at the Centre for this reason. Hence coalition politics leads to instability, although it also gives representation to regional and small parties.

subject: Political Science
stem: State whether the following statement is true or false and give the reason for your answer: Consumer movement came into existence.
solution: True. The consumer movement arose out of the exploitation of ordinary buyers in the market. Traders and producers indulged in adulteration of food, use of false weights and measures, charging more than the printed price, hoarding and black-marketing, the sale of unsafe and poor quality goods, misleading advertisements and the refusal of service after sale, while the individual consumer was scattered, unorganised and unable to fight a big company alone. To resist this exploitation consumers began to organise themselves into consumer associations, to spread awareness of consumer rights - the right to safety, to information, to choose, to be heard and to redressal - and to press the government for protection. As a result the Consumer Protection Act was passed in 1986, consumer courts, that is, consumer disputes redressal forums, were set up at the district, state and national levels, standards such as the ISI and Agmark were enforced, and 24th December is observed as National Consumer Day. Thus the consumer movement came into existence.

subject: Political Science
stem: Explain the following concept: Criminalisation of politics.
solution: Criminalisation of politics means the entry of criminals into politics and the use of criminal methods in the political process. Persons against whom serious criminal cases such as murder, extortion, kidnapping or corruption are pending contest elections, are given tickets by parties because their money and muscle power can win seats, and are elected to the legislatures; criminals are also used to capture polling booths, to threaten voters and rival candidates and to rig elections. The result is that law-breakers become law-makers, honest and capable candidates are pushed out, the police and the administration come under pressure, justice is obstructed and the faith of citizens in democracy is weakened. To check it, candidates are now required to declare their criminal cases, assets and educational qualifications in an affidavit at the time of nomination, fast-track courts have been set up for cases against legislators, and a convicted legislator is disqualified immediately.

subject: Political Science
stem: Explain the following concept: Rights based approach.
solution: The rights based approach is the approach in which the basic needs of the people are given to them not as charity or as a favour under a welfare scheme that the government may withdraw at will, but as legal rights which the citizen can claim as a matter of entitlement and can enforce in a court of law if they are denied. It shifts the citizen from the position of a beneficiary to that of a rights-holder and makes the government accountable to him. In India this approach was adopted in a big way after 2005 - the Right to Information Act of 2005, the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act of 2005 which guarantees the right to work, the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act of 2009 and the National Food Security Act of 2013 which gives the right to food. The rights based approach makes the administration transparent and responsible and thereby deepens democracy.

subject: Political Science
stem: Answer in brief: What is meant by establishment of social justice?
solution: Social justice means that every member of society should get equality of status and of opportunity and should be able to live with dignity, without being discriminated against on the ground of caste, religion, race, language, sex or economic position. Establishment of social justice therefore means building such a society by deliberate effort of the state and of the people - by guaranteeing the Fundamental Rights of equality before law and equality of opportunity, by abolishing untouchability and forbidding discrimination, by following the Directive Principles which ask the state to reduce inequalities of income and status, by providing reservation for the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes in education, in government service and in legislatures, by making special provisions for women, children, the disabled and the minorities, and by running welfare schemes of education, employment, housing and health for the weaker sections. Its aim is to bring the exploited and neglected sections of society into the mainstream and to remove age-old injustice.

subject: Political Science
stem: Answer in brief: What is meant by midterm elections?
solution: The Lok Sabha and the Vidhan Sabhas are elected for a fixed term of five years, and elections are normally held at the end of that term, which are called general elections. Sometimes, however, the ruling party or coalition loses its majority in the House, or the government resigns, or the House is dissolved by the President or the Governor before the completion of five years. In such a case the House cannot continue, and fresh elections have to be held before the scheduled time in order to constitute a new House. Elections held in this way in the middle of the term are called midterm elections. They must be distinguished from a by-election, which is held only for one seat that has fallen vacant because of the death or resignation of a member.
